title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
abstract: Abstract Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues. This mechanism enables cells to efficiently fight oxidative stress. Under oxidative stress, cells execute a metabolic shift, blocking glycolytic flux into the TCA cycle to shunt glycolytic carbons toward the pentose phosphate pathway. This generates NADPH which cells use to detoxify H 2 O 2 and to reduce oxidized cysteines. We find that DLAT oxidation is required for cells to mount an effective antioxidant response. Mutations preventing DLAT oxidation render PDH resistant to oxidative inhibition, impair NADPH generation, reduce peroxide detoxification, and sensitize cells to oxidative damage and death. DLAT oxidation also drives a Warburg-like metabolic phenotype of increased glucose uptake, elevated lactate secretion, and reduced TCA cycle activity. Thus DLAT oxidation is a redox-sensing mechanism that regulates PDH activity and central carbon metabolism.

title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
abstract: Abstract The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. To resolve this problem, we hypothesize the existence of simpler HK97-fold viral capsids associated with smaller genomes than those of known HK97-fold viruses. Such small viral genomes are searched in environmental metagenomes across public databases, including IMG/M and MGnify. Using hidden Markov models and protein language models, we identify and characterize small viral genomes encoding HK97-fold proteins that exhibit molecular similarities to encapsulins yet lack portal and tail genes. The phylogenetic analyses of HK97-fold proteins reveal independent mixed groups of viruses and encapsulins, and structural analyses identify similarities between encapsulins and procapsids, the immature state of viral capsids. The observations support a bidirectional evolution between encapsulins and HK97-fold viruses enabled by the viral procapsid state. Using biophysical and genomic arguments, we introduce an evolutionary model of HK97-fold protein shells, predicting that they emerged as lower-symmetry biochemical compartments and that HK97-fold viral capsids may retain biochemical functions.

title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
abstract: Abstract Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

title: Association Between Local Factors and Implant‐Related Complications: A Population‐Sampled Cross‐Sectional Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To investigate the role of local factors and the association with peri‐implantitis and peri‐implant soft‐tissue dehiscence (PISTD). Materials and Methods A randomly selected sample of Norwegian patients who underwent implant therapy in 2014 was examined (242 patients; 732 implants). Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded, including soft‐tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, connection type, platform switching, emergence angle, implant location and presence of adjacent teeth. To account for clustering of implants within patients, mixed‐effects logistic regression models were applied. Results Mucosal margin mobility, bone‐level implants without platform switching, emergence angle > 45°, anterior implant location and daily smoking were identified as significant risk indicators for peri‐implantitis. Thin soft‐tissue phenotype, mucosal margin mobility, absence of adjacent teeth, peri‐implantitis and external connection were detected as significant indicators for PISTD. Peri‐implantitis and PISTD were present in 8.7% and 25.0% of implants, respectively. Conclusions Local factors and soft‐tissue‐related parameters, many modifiable during treatment planning, were associated with peri‐implantitis and PISTD. Particular attention should be given to soft‐tissue phenotype, connection design, platform switching and prosthetic emergence angle. The relationship between systemic and local risk factors should be further investigated.

title: Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study
abstract: Abstract Despite growing clinical adoption of artificial intelligence in radiology, fewer than one in five commercially available models are cleared for paediatric use. Existing systems are trained predominantly on adult data and generalize poorly to neonates, yet efficient strategies for repurposing them without data sharing or large-scale local data curation are lacking. Here we present an international retrospective study of neonatal chest radiographs from 30 neonatal intensive care units across 20 countries and territories, evaluating continual learning as a privacy-preserving approach to adapt a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care. Each hospital contributed 50 radiographs for sequential model retraining without centralized data pooling. Continual learning achieved lower anatomical landmark localization error (0.67 cm versus 1.29 cm for hospital-specific fine-tuning and 4.30 cm for adult-only models) at 29 of 30 sites, with improved detection of deep intubations at 27 of 30 sites. These findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving collaborative learning can address critical gaps in paediatric AI deployment.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
abstract: Abstract Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
abstract: Abstract Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

title: The Neural Symphony in the Periodontium: Health, Inflammation, and Regeneration
abstract: Periodontal nerves, comprising sensory, sympathetic, and parasympathetic fibers, are essential components of the periodontium. Beyond their classic sensory and proprioceptive functions, these neural networks actively modulate periodontal immune responses, bone remodeling, and tissue regeneration. They orchestrate tissue homeostasis by releasing specific neuropeptides, neurotransmitters, and neurotrophic factors. The progression of periodontitis is intimately linked to neural dysregulation, where proinflammatory mediators (e.g., excessive substance P and sympathetic catecholamines) overpower protective signals (e.g., calcitonin gene-related peptide and parasympathetic acetylcholine). Conversely, successful periodontal regeneration requires the restoration of this neural equilibrium. Nerve terminals rapidly sprout into osteogenic zones during early repair. Subsequently, their spatiotemporally patterned signaling suppresses osteoclastogenesis and promotes the osteogenic differentiation of stem cells. Crucially, these local neural networks function as a bidirectional conduit linking the periodontium to the central nervous system: systemic stressors (eg, sleep deprivation and chronic stress) can compromise ganglionic autophagy or trigeminal function to exacerbate periodontal bone loss, while periodontal pathogens can reciprocally exploit these pathways to induce central neuroinflammation. Recognizing this interconnected oral–neural–brain axis not only explains why certain periodontitis-susceptible patients remain refractory to conventional therapies but also highlights the broader impact of periodontal inflammation on neurodegenerative risk. Furthermore, nerve-targeted strategies, including neurotrophin-functionalized biomaterials, local neuropeptide delivery, and bioelectric neuromodulation, offer promising approaches to resolving refractory inflammation, restoring periodontal integrity, and concurrently mitigating the risk of associated central neuroinflammation. In this review, we comprehensively characterize the spatiotemporal plasticity of periodontal nerves under physiological and pathological conditions. We dissect the molecular mechanisms linking neural signaling to periodontal immunity and repair, and highlight how integrating neurobiology into periodontology could advance the development of next-generation regenerative medicine.

title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
abstract: Abstract Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

title: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
abstract: Abstract Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
abstract: Abstract Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51–DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B’s critical role in genome maintenance.

title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
abstract: Abstract Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.

title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
abstract: Abstract The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry
abstract: Abstract Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP’s promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
abstract: Abstract We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
abstract: Abstract Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
abstract: Abstract Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
abstract: Abstract Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
abstract: Abstract ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
abstract: Abstract Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
abstract: Abstract Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
abstract: Abstract Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
abstract: Abstract Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

title: Bi-allelic EPHA2 mutations cause dysosteosclerosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and enhancing osteoblastogenesis
abstract: Abstract Erythropoietin-producing hepatocellular (EPH) receptors, the largest receptor tyrosine kinase family, have been shown to play a crucial role in normal physiological processes and pathologies. EPHA2, encoded by EPHA2 gene, a member of the EPH receptor family, has been implicated in cataracts and various bone tumors, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and bone metastases of breast cancer. However, no association between the EPHA2 gene and genetic skeletal disorders has been reported to date. Here, we identified a Chinese family with a diagnosis of dysosteosclerosis, presenting with significant increase in lumbar spine bone mineral density, multifocal sclerotic lesions throughout the body, sclerotic skull, platyspondyly and sandwich vertebrae, and demonstrated compound heterozygous mutations in EPHA2 gene (c.890 C > T, p.Thr297Met; c.988dupT, p.Ser330PhefsX51). We observed a reduction in numerous sclerotic lesions in patients during the five-year follow-up. To systematically investigate the molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis, we employed a range of methodologies, including in vitro cellular assays, genome-wide association studies analysis, induced pluripotent stem cells models and Epha2 knockout mice models. We have determined that loss-of-function mutations in EPHA2 gene lead to dysosteosclerosis through enhancing mesenchymal stem cells osteogenic differentiation and downregulating the p38-MAPK pathway, leading to decreased osteoclast differentiation. Consequently, we proposed and validated EPHA2 as a viable therapeutic target for osteoporosis by constructing femoral fracture mice models and ovariectomized mice models. In summary, this study identifies bi-allelic loss-of-function mutations in EPHA2 gene lead to dysosteosclerosis and its underlying mechanisms, and suggests EPHA2 as a potential therapeutic target for osteoporosis.

title: Microbial Network Signatures Associated With Outcomes of Peri‐Implantitis Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To investigate the microbial network signatures associated with outcomes following surgical therapy of peri‐implantitis. Materials and Methods Microbiological data from a 1‐year randomised controlled trial of 28 patients (28 implants) were analysed. Based on a composite outcome (probing depth ≤ 5 mm, minimal bleeding on probing and no further marginal bone loss) at 1 year, implant sites were categorised into a successful ( n = 10) or a non‐successful group ( n = 18). Peri‐implant crevicular fluid was collected at baseline and at 3, 6 and 12 months and analysed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Results A significant compositional shift from baseline to 1 year was observed in the successful group ( p = 0.001), with a significant increase in Rothia aeria ( p = 0.048), Haemophilus parainfluenzae ( p = 0.033) and Neisseria oralis ( p = 0.025) over time. Network analysis revealed that the successful group exhibited a Porphyromonas gingivalis ‐associated module enriched with high‐centrality commensals at baseline, and significantly greater network edge density ( p = 0.005) and connectivity ( p = 0.018) at 1 year. Spearman correlation analyses at 1 year identified significant negative correlations between P. gingivalis and commensals including H. parainfluenzae , Streptococcus species and Veillonella undefined ( p < 0.05). Conclusion In this exploratory secondary analysis of a small cohort, favourable outcomes of peri‐implantitis therapy were associated with increased microbial network connectivity and commensal centrality. Trial Registration Korean Clinical Research Information Service number KCT0007900

title: Effect of Crestal Soft‐Tissue Augmentation Prior to or Simultaneously With Implant Placement on Peri‐Implant Tissue Dimensions: Histological Outcomes of an Experimental In Vivo Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To histologically assess the effect of the timing of soft‐tissue augmentation (prior to or simultaneously with implant placement) and the type of grafting material on peri‐implant soft‐tissue dimensions. Materials and Methods Mandibular molars (M1, M2, M3) were bilaterally extracted in six beagle dogs. Eight weeks after extraction, one mandibular side received primary soft‐tissue augmentation with an autogenous subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) or a collagen‐based graft substitute (CG x1D), or no augmentation. At Week 16, implants were placed at these sites without flap. On the contralateral side, implants were placed with flap elevation simultaneously with SCTG or CG x1D, or no augmentation. Animals were sacrificed at Week 36. Histometric outcomes were analysed using linear mixed‐effects models with dog as a random intercept; significant six‐group effects were followed by Tukey‐adjusted pairwise comparisons. Results All six groups showed crestal bone remodelling apical to the implant shoulder. The AFL group consistently exhibited the greatest peri‐implant soft‐tissue dimensions. Significant overall group effects were identified for lingual fBIC‐M ( F = 3.58, p = 0.014) and lingual IS‐M ( F = 4.46, p = 0.005), with AFL significantly exceeding FL and FC at both outcomes. SCTG sites showed significantly greater lingual fBIC‐M and IS‐M than collagen substitute sites ( p = 0.013 and p = 0.012, respectively). Conclusions Prior soft‐tissue augmentation with an autogenous graft before flapless implant placement (AFL) resulted in more favourable peri‐implant soft‐tissue dimensions. Both autogenous grafts and collagen substitutes contribute to soft‐tissue volume gains around implants. Clinical trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

title: Periodontal Treatment Restores Gingival Crevicular Fluid and Serum Periostin Levels
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aim To investigate the effect of periodontal treatment on periodontal inflammation and periostin levels in patients with severe periodontitis. Methods This study included two groups (periodontitis and periodontally healthy), each comprising 24 individuals. Periodontal clinical parameters were recorded, and serum samples were collected at baseline and on Days 30 and 90 following non‐surgical periodontal treatment (NSPT). Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) samples were collected at baseline and on Days 1, 2, 14, 30 and 90 following NSPT. Periostin, interleukin‐1 beta (IL‐1β) and fibroblast growth factor‐2 (FGF‐2) levels were assessed in serum and GCF samples. Results Clinical periodontal parameters decreased from baseline to Days 30 and 90 after NSPT ( p = 0.001). Patients with periodontitis had higher levels of IL‐1β in serum ( p = 0.020) and GCF ( p = 0.001) than healthy individuals. Following periodontal treatment, serum IL‐1β levels decreased at Days 30 ( p = 0.036) and 90 ( p = 0.025) while GCF IL‐1β levels showed a reduction at Day 14 ( p = 0.001). Periostin levels in GCF in patients with periodontitis were lower than in healthy individuals at baseline ( p = 0.001). It increased after treatment, reaching peak values on Day 14 ( p = 0.001), followed by a gradual decrease on Days 30 ( p = 0.007) and 90 ( p = 0.001). Levels of FGF‐2 in GCF increased after periodontal treatment compared with baseline in patients with periodontitis, reaching peak levels on Day 2 ( p = 0.001). Following periodontal treatment, periostin and FGF‐2 levels remained higher in the periodontitis group than in the healthy group ( p < 0.05), whereas IL‐1β levels decreased to levels comparable to those of the healthy group by Day 30 ( p ≥ 0.05). Conclusion In parallel with the reduction in periodontal tissue inflammation and IL‐1β, periostin levels in GCF increased in response to periodontal treatment, suggesting its involvement in tissue healing in patients with periodontitis.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
abstract: Abstract Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Abstract Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Abstract Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Abstract Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
abstract: Abstract Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
abstract: Abstract Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
abstract: Abstract Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
abstract: Abstract Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
abstract: Abstract Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
abstract: Abstract Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
abstract: Abstract Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
abstract: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

title: AI-assisted scoping review of code sharing in clinical prediction model research
abstract: Abstract Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings.

title: Human-specific morphoregulatory signatures in basal radial glia characterise neocortex evolution
abstract: Abstract As the seat of our cognition, the human neocortex is an object of immense fascination. Human neocortex expansion during evolution has been attributed to an increase in the proliferative capacity of neural progenitor cells during development, particularly basal radial glia. Despite their evolutionary relevance, the genomic changes driving human basal radial glia biology remain uncharacterised. We use comparative chromatin and transcriptional profiling of neural progenitor cells isolated from gorilla, chimpanzee and human cerebral organoids to identify cis-regulatory elements that have gained activity in humans. Focusing specifically on basal radial glia, we discover that morphoregulatory enhancer activity and gene expression signatures distinguish human basal radial glia from other great apes. Functional analysis of the morphoregulatory genes FAM107A and CNGA3 in human organoids reveals that these genes contribute to the morphological complexity of human basal radial glia. Taken together, our inter-species comparison of basal radial glia suggests that human-specific morphoregulatory signatures characterise neocortex evolution.
